create.name: CuCe-1
create.synthesis_para: The Cu0.15Ce0.85O2−y mixed oxide sample was synthesized by co-precipitation according to the procedure described in the literature [6]. Briefly, the sample was obtained from well-mixed (stirrer speed of 4000 rpm) Cu(NO3)2 · 3H2O (99.5 wt% purity, Merck) and Ce(NO3)3 · 6H2O (99 wt% purity, Aldrich) solutions by dropping the solution of sodium carbonate (Na2CO3 · 10H2O, 99 wt% purity, Kemika, Croatia) and keeping the pH below 5.5 as described in detail in [14]. The precipitate was filtered, thoroughly washed with hot distilled water, dried overnight at 110 ◦C, and calcined in a dry air flow at 500 ◦C for 1 h to prepare a mixed oxide sample. The formulation Cu0.15Ce0.85O2−y means that Cu/(Cu + Ce) = 0.15 and Ce/(Cu + Ce) = 0.85 (the mole fractions of copper and cerium, respectively)

create.name: CuCe-2
create.synthesis_para: Two CuxCe1−xO2−y oxide samples, where x varies as 0.15 (CuCe-2) and 0.10 (CuCe-2a), were prepared by the sol–gel peroxide route method [15] by reacting CuCl2 · 2H2O (99 wt% purity, Aldrich) with an H2O2 water solution (30 wt%, p.a., Merck) and in a separate vessel by reacting H2O2 water solution with CeCl3 · 7H2O (99.9 wt% purity, Aldrich). The concentration of each metal chloride in aqueous H2O2 solutions was altered to attain the desired (Cu:Ce) molar ratio in the oxide samples. After the reactions in both vessels were completed, the two solutions were vigorously mixed and the excess peroxide was decomposed at about 60 ◦C and then the ethanol was added slowly during continuous stirring at room temperature. The solvent was removed by evaporation at about 40 ◦C, and then the remaining viscous product was slowly dried to obtain the xerogel, which was calcined at 400 ◦C for 6 h in dry air.

create.name: Ce0.9Pr0.1O2-reference
create.synthesis_para: The metal precursors were dissolved in 9:1 molar ratio in ethyleneglycol (total concentration 2.4 g/mL) and methanol was added (0.13 gmethanol/gethyleneglycol dissolution). For Ce0.9Pr0.1O2-infiltrated preparation, this solution was dropped to the colloidal crystal template avoiding excess of liquid, and the impregnated template was dried at 100 °C overnight. For Ce0.9Pr0.1O2-reference preparation, the dissolution was dried overnight in the same conditions (without impregnation). Finally, both solids were calcined at 500 °C for 2 h with a heating rate of 1 °C/min.

create.name: CH0
create.synthesis_para: Stoichiometric ratios of metal precursors were added in such a way that the composition of HfO2 on CeO2 varies from 0 to 100 mol % with 10 mol % difference between each sample. Synthesis procedure of EDTA-Citrate complexing method was followed as reported previously [16,23]. Oven drying of the obtained gel at 150 °C/24 h resulted in the formation of black precursor solid. Further, two-stage calcinations at 350 °C/12 h and 600 °C/5 h were carried out to get the corresponding metal oxide nanomaterials. The obtained metal oxides, CexHf1-xO2 (where x = 0.0–1.0) was represented as CHx where x varies from 0 to 100 where, CH0 and CH100 correspond to CeO2 and HfO2, respectively.

create.name: SDC15
create.synthesis_para: Gd/Sm-doped ceria samples with composition of Ce1 − xGd / SmxO2 − δ for (x = 0.05 to 0.30) were prepared by co-precipitation method using ammonium oxalate as the precipitating agent. Table 1 lists various compositions and their nomenclature used in the present work. All the chemicals were used as received without further purifications. The stock solution was made by dissolving cerium nitrate hexahydrate (Ce(NO3)3·6H2O Sigma Aldrich 99.9% purity), gadolinium nitrate hexahydrate (Gd(NO3)3·6H2O Sigma Aldrich 99.9% purity) and samarium nitrate hexahydrate (Sm(NO3)3·6H2O Sigma Aldrich 99.9% purity) in double distilled water of various molar ratio (x = 0.05 to 0.30) of dopant to cerium. Aqueous solutions of ammonium oxalate (NH4)2C2O4·H2) and 99.5% Merck with a concentration of 0.3 M were used as precipitating agent. In a typical procedure, 50 ml mixed salt solution was added at a rate of 5 ml/min into 150 ml oxalate solution under vigorous stirring at room temperature where white precipitate formed instantaneously. The resultant suspension was homogenenized for 1 h and then centrifuged at 7000 rpm for 15 min to separate precipitate from solvent. The precipitate was washed repeatedly with distilled water and ethanol, followed by drying at 80 °C to obtain the GDC/SDC oxalate precursor. Finally, the precursors were calcined at 400 °C in air for 3 h to convert into crystalline form

create.name: 5% La CeO2
create.synthesis_para: Nanostructured CeCO3OH particles was synthesized by a simple hydrothermal method which can be found in our previous work (Mao et al. 2021a). Briefly, 0.790 g of NH4HCO3 was added in 20 mL of distilled water together with 7 mL of ethanol, 0.434 g of cerium nitrate and 0, 5, 10, or 15 mol. % of La(NO3)3·6H2O, Y(NO3)3·6H2O, or Sm(NO3)3·6H2O, were dissolved into 10 mL of distilled water. The two solutions were stirred for 30 min then transferred into a 100 mL Teflon lined stainless steel autoclave and heated at 115 °C for 8 h. After cooling down to the room temperature, the precipitate was washed with distilled water and ethanol for several times, and then dried at 35 °C for 12 h in a vacuum oven. The obtained powders were thereby named as X % RE CeCO3OH. The synthesized CeCO3OH was placed in a ceramic boat and then maintained in a tube furnace, before a calcination in H2, the air in tube furnace was repeatedly expelled out by alternately flowing argon and vacuuming for several times. Then, a 1.6 L/min of hydrogen was flowed into the tube furnace and the temperature was raised from room temperature to 600 °C then kept at 600 °C for 2 h to obtain X % RE CeO2, where X % was the mole ratio of RE (La, Sm, and Y) and Ce.

create.name: Ce0.9Co0.1O2
create.synthesis_para: Preparation of mesoporous CeO2–Co3O4 mixed oxides, ceria, and Co3O4 was carried out using modified template-assisted method [38]. Cerium(III)nitrate hexahydrate (Ce(NO3)3.6H2O) and cobalt(II)nitrate hexahydrate (Co(NO3)2.6H2O) of Sigma-Aldrich AR grade were used as precursors and poly(ethylene glycol)-block-poly(propylene glycol)-block-poly(ethylene glycol) (P123) polymer was used as template. In typical procedure, desired amounts of Ce(NO3)3.6H2O, Co(NO3)2.6H2O, and 1-butanol were taken in a beaker, and desirable amount of P123 was added. While stirring, required amount of concentrated nitric acid was added to the above solution at room temperature until contents dissolved. Then the solution was heated to 120 °C on oil bath and stirring continued for 3 h at that temperature. After that obtained black powder was washed with ethanol several times to remove anion impurities, centrifuged, and dried at 120 °C for 12 h. Dried samples were calcinated with different heating cycles. After heating at 150 °C for 12 h, cooled to room temperature, then heated at 250 °C for 4 h, 350 °C for 3 h, 450 °C for 2 h, and 550 °C for 1 h.

create.name: CeO2:2.5% Y3+
create.synthesis_para: Undoped and the three different trivalent rare-earths (Y3+ , Eu3+ and La3+) doped CeO2 samples were synthesized via gel combustion method using cerium nitrate hexahydrate and urea as the oxidant and fuel, respectively. The fuel to oxidant ratio was kept at 2:1 for all the samples. The trivalent ion doping was carried out at two different molar concentrations of 2.5% and 5% w.r.t. the number of moles of ceria To prepare the Y3+ and La3+ doped ceria samples, stoichiometric amounts of lanthanum nitrate hexahydrate and yttrium nitrate were directly added to the precursor mixture, whereas to synthesize the Eu3+ doped samples initially a stock solution of Eu3+ was prepared by dissolving Eu2O3 in dil. HNO3 and then requisite amount of that solution was added to the fuel-oxidant mixture. The sample solutions were heated under the IR lamp for approximately an hour to get converted into the gel form. The gel was then initially ignited for few minutes at 250 °C for the combustion of urea, followed by crushing, calcinations for three hours at 500 °C and then finally annealed at 800 °C for four hours.

create.name: 10Zr:CeO2
create.synthesis_para: Pure ceria sample and ceria samples doped with 10, 20, and 30 mol. % of zirconium, denoted CeO2, 10Zr:CeO2, 20Zr:CeO2, and 30Zr:CeO2, respectively, were prepared using combustion synthesis with cerium nitrate hexahydrate, Ce(NO3)3·6H2O (p.a., Acros Organics, Geel, Belgium) and zirconium oxynitrate n-hydrate, ZrO(NO3)2·nH2O (p.a., Merck, Germany) as oxidants, and glycine (p.a., Lachner, Neratovice, Czech Republic) as fuel. The appropriate amounts of precursors were calculated based on equation 1 and placed in a porcelain bowl with 10 mL of demineralized water. The aqueous mixture of precursors was stirred at 300 rpm and 60 °C until the water evaporated and a viscous sludge remained. The mixture was then relocated into a sand bath inside a fume hood; the temperature of the sand bath was set to maximum (700 °C) and the temperature of the reaction mixture was monitored with an IR pyrometer. After the combustion reaction, evidenced by an intense yellow flame and the release of a large amount of gases, a fine yellow powder product of low density remained. The yellow color became brighter as the amount of added zirconium increases. The as-prepared samples were thermally treated at 500 °C for 2 h in order to gain insight in the thermal stability of the samples and potential crystallization of impurities or zirconium-based phases, as well as to prepare them for the catalytic activity test, since 500 °C is the maximum temperature expected to be reached during the tests, based on our previous research regarding VOCs oxidation with the use of ceria-based nanocatalysts [18].

create.name: Ce0.75Y0.25O2-δ
create.synthesis_para: A citrate-complexation method was employed to synthesize nano-scale CeO2 and Ce0.75RE0.25O2-δ (RE = Y, Sm and La) composite oxides in this paper. In a typical synthesis batch, the calculated amounts of Ce(NO3)3·6H2O, RE(NO3)3·6H2O and citric acid were dissolved in deionized water and stirred at 60 °C for 5 min to get clear and homogenous mixture solution, and the molar ratio of metal ions to citrate was fixed at 1.0. Then, the resulting mixture solution was transferred into a microwave muffle furnace (Phoenix standard unit; CEM Corporation in USA) and calcined at 500 °C for 2 h to obtain the final catalyst samples (Ce0.75RE0.25O2-δ and CeO2). Accordingly, the whole time for the synthesis of catalysts was substantially shortened within 3 h.

create.synthesis_para: Polycrystalline Ce-1xFexO2 (for x = 0.00, 0.05 and 0.10) samples were prepared using the conventional low-temperature solid-state reaction route. In the solid-state diffusion process, the stoichiometric proportions of cerium oxide and iron powders (purity better than 4N, purchased from Sigma Aldrich) were mixed thoroughly using an agate pestle and mortar and then calcinated for 15 h at 500 °C in a microprocessor controlled furnace. The obtained polycrystalline precursors were crushed to a fine powder form and then were pressed into Pellets using a hydraulic pressure of nearly 6 tons and then sintered at 500 °C in Ar atmosphere.

Citric acid was added as complex agent, and glycol was used as additive. After continuous stirring for 2 h, the mixed solution was treated at the temperature of 353 K overnight to form the sponge yellow gel. Then, the gel was dried at 373 K for 3 h and milled before calcination. The dried gel was calcined at 573 K for 30 min and then at 773 K for 5 h. In this way, the fresh sample was obtained.
